verses.text: After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward."
But Abram replied, "O Lord GOD, what can You give me, since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?"
Abram continued, "Behold, You have given me no offspring, so a servant in my household will be my heir."
Then the word of the LORD came to Abram, saying, "This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir."
And the LORD took him outside and said, "Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able." Then He told him, "So shall your offspring be."
Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
The LORD also told him, "I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess."
But Abram replied, "Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?"
And the LORD said to him, "Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon."
So Abram brought all these to Him, split each of them down the middle, and laid the halves opposite each other. The birds, however, he did not cut in half.
And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him.
Then the LORD said to Abram, "Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will depart with many possessions.
You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.
In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete."
When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, behold, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared and passed between the halves of the carcasses.
On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, "To your descendants I have given this land—from the river of Egypt to the great River Euphrates—
the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,
Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaites,
Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites."

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Family narrative: the story of Abraham, Sarah and their family (Genesis 11:27 to 25:11)
context.audience: Israel, the children of Abraham, learning how God’s promise began
context.setting: The word of the LORD comes to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward” (v.1). Abram answers that he is still childless, and his heir will be Eliezer of Damascus, a servant (vv.2-3). God says his heir will come from his own body, takes him outside and says, “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able… So shall your offspring be” (vv.4-5). “Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness” (v.6). Asked how he can know he will possess the land, Abram is told to bring a heifer, a goat, a ram, a dove and a pigeon; he cuts the animals in two and drives away the birds of prey (vv.8-11). As the sun sets, a deep sleep and great darkness fall on him, and God tells him his descendants will be strangers and slaves in another land for four hundred years and then come out with great possessions (vv.12-16). After dark “a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared and passed between the halves of the carcasses” (v.17), and the LORD makes a covenant giving Abram’s descendants the land “from the river of Egypt to the great River Euphrates” (v.18).
context.custom: In the ancient Near East a covenant could be sealed by cutting animals in two and walking between the halves, as if to say, ‘May this be done to me if I break my word’ (compare Jeremiah 34:18). Treaties found at Mari and among the Hittites and Assyrians use similar rites. Here only God, in fire and smoke, passes between the pieces: He alone takes the oath. Tablets from Nuzi show that a childless man could adopt a servant as his heir, which may lie behind v.3.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 16 tells how Sarai gave her servant Hagar to Abram, and Hagar bore Ishmael.
context.timelineBible: Paul builds his teaching on v.6: “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness” (Romans 4:3), before he was circumcised (Romans 4:10), so he is the father of all who believe (Galatians 3:6-7). James quotes the same verse and points to Abraham’s obedience in offering Isaac (James 2:21-23). Stephen recalls the four hundred years in Egypt (Acts 7:6-7).

translation.meaning: To be firm, to trust, to believe. The root of ‘amen.’ Abram leaned his whole weight on God’s word.
Righteousness: being right with God and doing right. God counted Abram’s trust as righteousness.
To cut. In Hebrew one ‘cuts’ a covenant, and here the animals were literally cut in two.

gospelParallels.note: Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
Those who have faith are sons of Abraham.
Enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.

otBackground.note: The calf they cut in two and walked between.
You, O LORD, are a shield around me.

overview.summary: God promises the childless Abram a son and offspring as many as the stars; Abram believes and it is counted to him as righteousness; then God seals His promise of the land by passing alone, as fire and smoke, between the halves of the sacrificed animals.
overview.settingLine: Under the night sky at Mamre.

history.t: Nuzi tablets show servants adopted as heirs.
Animals cut in two to seal an oath.

customs.t: About 3,000 stars can be seen by eye on a dark night.

archaeology.t: Texts from Mari on the Euphrates (18th century BC) speak of killing a donkey to make a covenant.
Family contracts from Nuzi in northern Iraq (15th century BC) on adoption and inheritance.

overview.discussion: “Abram believed the LORD” (v.6) before he saw a single descendant. What promise of God am I being asked to believe before I can see it?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters (1-25 in the app so far). Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham and his family.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

peoplePlaces.d: The servant who would have been heir
